metadata.title: Build an AI Daily Briefing with n8n
metadata.description: Build a self-hosted workflow that collects, ranks, summarizes, and emails the most important AI and technology news.

outcomes: Deploy a persistent n8n instance with Docker Compose on Ubuntu.
Retrieve and normalize current AI news with Tavily Search.
Filter, deduplicate, rank, and batch articles for AI processing.
Generate validated structured summaries and HTML with Gemini and JavaScript.
Deliver the briefing through Gmail manually and on a daily schedule.
requirements: Tavily and Google AI Studio accounts
Google Cloud and Gmail accounts for email delivery

assets.alt: Preview of the completed AI Daily Briefing
AI Daily Briefing workflow from search to inbox

overview.heading: Build an AI Daily Briefing
paragraphs: Build a self-hosted AI Daily Briefing system on Ubuntu.

n8n orchestrates the workflow: Tavily retrieves current technology news, the pipeline cleans and ranks the results, Gemini analyzes and summarizes the most important stories, and Gmail delivers the final HTML briefing.
The finished system supports both manual testing and scheduled daily execution.

steps.title: Collect
steps.description: Tavily Search retrieves recent AI and technology news from the web.

steps.title: Process
steps.description: n8n normalizes, filters, deduplicates, sorts, and limits the collected articles.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: Gemini scores importance, rewrites headlines, summarizes stories, and assigns categories.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.description: JavaScript validates the response and builds the HTML briefing before Gmail sends it.

finalOutcome.heading: Final Outcome
finalOutcome.description: A reproducible local workflow that delivers a daily AI briefing automatically while retaining a Manual Trigger for testing.

modules.title: Configure the Runtime Environment
modules.description: Install Docker and launch a persistent n8n service on Ubuntu.

lessons.title: Install Docker
objectives: Configure Docker's official Ubuntu repository.
Install Docker Engine and Docker Compose, then enable the service.

activity.prompt: Install Docker Engine and Compose, then confirm that the Docker service is enabled and running.

lessons.content:
# 1.1 Install Docker

Install Docker Engine and Compose from Docker’s official Ubuntu repository:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y ca-certificates curl

sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings

sudo curl -fsSL \
  https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \
  -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.sources > /dev/null <<EOF
Types: deb
URIs: https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu
Suites: $(. /etc/os-release && echo "${UBUNTU_CODENAME:-$VERSION_CODENAME}")
Components: stable
Architectures: $(dpkg --print-architecture)
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
EOF

sudo apt update

sudo apt install -y \
  docker-ce \
  docker-ce-cli \
  containerd.io \
  docker-buildx-plugin \
  docker-compose-plugin

sudo systemctl enable --now docker
```

lessons.title: Install and Start n8n
objectives: Create a persistent Docker volume and Compose configuration for n8n.
Start n8n, verify its readiness endpoint, and create the owner account.

activity.prompt: Start the n8n container, verify its readiness endpoint, and open localhost:5678 successfully.

lessons.content:
# 1.2 Install and Start n8n

```bash
mkdir -p ~/aivirteach/ai-daily-briefing

cd ~/aivirteach/ai-daily-briefing

sudo docker volume create ai_daily_briefing_n8n_data

nano compose.yaml

sudo docker compose config

sudo docker compose up -d

sudo docker compose ps

curl --noproxy "*" -fsS \
  http://127.0.0.1:5678/healthz/readiness >/dev/null \
  && echo "n8n is ready"
```

Paste this into `compose.yaml`:

```yaml
services:
  n8n:
    image: docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.31.7

    container_name: ai-daily-briefing-n8n

    restart: unless-stopped

    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5678:5678"

    environment:
      TZ: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur

      GENERIC_TIMEZONE: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur

      N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS: "true"

      N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED: "true"

    volumes:
      - ai_daily_briefing_n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n

volumes:
  ai_daily_briefing_n8n_data:
    external: true
```

Save and exit Nano: press `Ctrl + O`, press `Enter`, and then press `Ctrl + X`.

Open [http://localhost:5678](http://localhost:5678), create the owner account, and **Create Workflow**.

objectives: Add a Manual Trigger to a new workflow.
Use repeatable manual execution while building.

lessons.title: Retrieve News with Tavily
objectives: Create and secure a Tavily API credential.
Retrieve recent AI and technology news.

activity.prompt: Run the Tavily node and confirm it returns a non-empty results array.

lessons.content:
# 2.2 Retrieve News from the Internet

Create an account at [Tavily](https://app.tavily.com), copy the private `tvly-...` key, then add a Tavily **node→ Search** node and save the key as a Tavily API credential.

```
Resource: Search

Operation: Query
Query: latest important developments in artificial intelligence, AI models, semiconductors, cybersecurity, and technology companies

Topic: News
Search Depth: Basic
Days: 1
Max Results: 10
```

Execute the node.

lessons.title: Organize the News Data
objectives: Split Tavily results into individual items.
Normalize six article fields for downstream processing.

activity.prompt: Confirm every output item contains only the six normalized fields.

lessons.title: Clean, Deduplicate, Sort, and Limit Articles
objectives: Remove incomplete, duplicate, and previously processed articles.
Rank, limit, and aggregate candidates for Gemini.

activity.prompt: Run the processing chain and confirm Aggregate outputs one articles list containing no more than five candidates.

lessons.content:
# 2.4 Clean, Deduplicate, Sort, and Limit Candidate Articles

Add and execute these nodes in order:

Add Filter node: 

```
{{ $json.title }}   | String | is not empty (AND)
{{ $json.link }}    | String | is not empty (AND)
{{ $json.summary }} | String | is not empty
```

Add Remove Duplicates node: `Operation = Remove Items Repeated Within Current Input`

Add Remove Duplicates node: `Operation = Remove Item Processed in Previous Executions` 

Add Sort node: `Type = Simple`; `Field Name = score`; `Order = Descending` 

Add Limit node: `Max Items = 5`; `Keep = First Items`

Add Aggregate node:`Aggregate = All Item Data (Into a Single List)`; `Put Output in Field = articles`; `Include = Specified Fields`; `Fields = title, link, summary, source, publishedAt, score`

lessons.title: Generate Structured Summaries with Gemini
objectives: Call Gemini from an authenticated HTTP Request node.
Constrain the model to return ranked and categorized JSON.

activity.prompt: Execute the Gemini request and verify it returns structured JSON for every candidate article.

lessons.content:
# 2.5 Use Gemini to Generate Structured News Summaries

Add a HTTP Request node:

```
Method: POST
URL: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite:generateContent
Authentication: Generic Credential Type → Header Auth
Header: x-goog-api-key = your Google AI Studio API key (Create the API key in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys))
Allowed HTTP Request Domains: All
Send Body: On
Body Content Type: JSON
Specify Body: Using JSON
```

JSON: 

```jsx
{{ JSON.stringify({

  contents: [
    {
      parts: [
        {
          text: `You are an English technology news editor creating a daily AI briefing.

Analyze every candidate article supplied below.

Candidate articles:

${JSON.stringify($json.articles, null, 2)}

For each article:

1. Assign an importanceScore from 1 to 10.
2. Rewrite the headline in clear English using no more than 20 words.
3. Write an English summary containing 40 to 80 words.
4. Assign exactly one category from:
   AI
   Chips
   Tech Business
   Cybersecurity
   Other
5. Write one concise English sentence explaining why the article is important.
6. Preserve the original source, publishedAt, and link exactly.
7. Use only information contained in the supplied article.
8. Do not invent facts, statistics, quotations, organizations, products, or conclusions.
9. Return one result for every supplied article.

Return exactly this JSON structure:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "importanceScore": 1,
      "headline": "",
      "summary": "",
      "category": "",
      "reason": "",
      "source": "",
      "publishedAt": "",
      "link": ""
    }
  ]
}

Return JSON only.
Do not use Markdown.
Do not wrap the response in a code block.`
        }
      ]
    }
  ],

  generationConfig: {

    responseMimeType: "application/json",

    maxOutputTokens: 4000
  }

}) }}
```

Execute the step.

lessons.title: Parse Gemini Output and Generate the Briefing
objectives: Validate Gemini's response in an n8n Code node.
Generate the email subject and HTML briefing.

activity.prompt: Run the Code node and inspect the generated subject and HTML briefing.

lessons.content:
# 2.6 Parse Gemini Output and Generate the AI Daily Briefing

Add a Code node: `Mode = Run Once for All Items`; `Language = JavaScript`. 

Download the source file below, open it, and paste the complete contents into the Code node:

[AI_Daily_Briefing_Code.txt](AI_Daily_Briefing_Gemini_Code_No_Comments.txt)

Execute the node.

lessons.title: Send the Email and Enable Daily Automatic Execution
objectives: Configure Gmail OAuth with the gmail.send scope.
Send a test briefing, add a daily Schedule Trigger, and publish the workflow.

activity.prompt: Deliver a test briefing, enable the daily schedule, retain the Manual Trigger, and publish the workflow.

lessons.content:
# 2.7 Send the Email and Enable Daily Automatic Execution

Add a Gmail node and create an OAuth credential

1. In [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) → My first project = `named by n8n Gmail Automation` → create → APIs & Services → library → search and enable Gmail API
2. google auth platform → get started → app name = `n8n Gmail Automation` → User support email = xxx@gmail.com → next → external → next → Developer support email = xxx@gmail.com → next → create
3. test users → add users = xxx@gmail.com
4. data access → Add or remove scopes → add “`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`” → update → save
5. clients → create → Application type = Web application → Name = `n8n Gmail Client` → Authorized redirect URIs = `http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback`→ create
6. audience → publish app → confirm 
7. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from clients into n8n, save and sign in with Google

Configure the Gmail node:

```
Resource: Message
Operation: Send
To: recipient email address
Subject: {{ $json.subject }}
Email Type: HTML
Message: {{ $json.html }}
```

Execute once and verify the email. 

Then add Schedule Trigger node in front of Tavily node: 

```
Trigger Interval: Days
Days Between Triggers: 1
Trigger at Hour: 8
Trigger at Minute: 0
```

Keep the Manual Trigger node for future manual testing.

After confirming that the workflow runs successfully, click Publish to enable scheduled execution.

metadata.title: Build an AI Web Watcher Agent with n8n
metadata.description: Monitor a public webpage, detect meaningful changes, use Gemini to judge relevance, and send alerts through Gmail.

outcomes: Deploy n8n and a controlled test site with Docker Compose.
Retrieve and normalize public webpage content responsibly.
Persist snapshots and stop early when content has not changed.
Use Gemini structured output to classify relevant changes.
Send relevant Gmail alerts and maintain a responsible monitoring schedule.
requirements: 2 vCPUs, 4 GB memory, and 10 GB free storage
Google AI Studio and Google Cloud accounts
A public page whose terms allow automated access

overview.heading: Build an AI Web Watcher Agent
paragraphs: Build a self-hosted agent that monitors an allowed public webpage and detects meaningful changes.
n8n retrieves and normalizes the page, compares it with a stored snapshot, and sends real changes to Gemini for relevance analysis.
Relevant changes produce a concise Gmail alert; irrelevant and unchanged pages produce no email.

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.description: n8n checks a public webpage manually or on a responsible schedule.

steps.title: Normalize
steps.description: JavaScript converts noisy HTML into stable readable text.

steps.title: Compare
steps.description: The workflow compares the current page with its previous snapshot.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: Gemini judges whether the change matches the stated interest.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.description: Relevant changes send one Gmail alert before the snapshot advances.

finalOutcome.heading: Final Outcome
finalOutcome.description: A persistent webpage monitor that alerts you only when an allowed public page changes in a way you care about.

modules.title: Configure the Runtime Environment
modules.description: Verify Ubuntu and networking, install Docker, and launch n8n with a controlled test webpage.

lessons.title: Verify the Virtual Machine Environment
objectives: Confirm a supported Ubuntu LTS release and 64-bit architecture.
Check CPU, memory, storage, time, and sudo access.

activity.prompt: Run all VM checks and correct the time zone if necessary.

lessons.content:
# 1.1 Verify the Virtual Machine Environment

The environment recommended for this tutorial:

```
Operating system: 64-bit Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, or 26.04 LTS
CPU: 2 vCPUs or more
Memory: 4 GB or more
Free storage: 10 GB or more
Access: a user account with sudo permission
```

---

On Ubuntu Desktop, press `Ctrl + Alt + T` to open Terminal. A typical prompt looks like `username@computer-name:~$`:

- `username`: the account currently signed in
- `computer-name`: the virtual machine name
- `~`: the current directory is the user's home directory
- `$`: the terminal is ready for a command

Do not copy the `$` prompt symbol. Copy and run each complete code block:

```bash
# Display the current Linux distribution, version, and codename
cat /etc/os-release
# Confirm that ID=ubuntu appears

# Display the processor architecture
uname -m
# x86_64 and aarch64 are common 64-bit architectures

# Display the number of logical CPUs
nproc

# Display memory usage in human-readable units
free -h
# available shows the approximate memory currently available to applications

# Check the root filesystem capacity and remaining space
df -h /
# Avail is the remaining space; Use% is the disk usage percentage

# Display the time, time zone, and synchronization status
timedatectl

# Verify that the current user has administrative access
sudo -v
# No characters appear while the password is typed; this is normal
```

**Check the result**

Confirm that Ubuntu is detected, the architecture is 64-bit, at least two CPUs and about 4 GB memory are available, the root filesystem has enough free space, the clock is correct, and `sudo -v` returns without an error.

If the time zone is incorrect, set it before continuing:

```bash
sudo timedatectl set-timezone Asia/Kuala_Lumpur
timedatectl
```

lessons.title: Verify the Network Environment
objectives: Verify interface, route, DNS, and HTTPS connectivity.
Choose an allowed API or feed instead of bypassing access controls.

activity.prompt: Test every required hostname and service, then diagnose any failing layer.

lessons.content:
# 1.2 Verify the Network Environment

Network checks are divided into four levels:

```
Network interface
      ↓
Default route
      ↓
DNS name resolution
      ↓
HTTPS service access
```

---

```bash
# View network devices and their connection status
nmcli device status

# Display interfaces and IP addresses in a concise format
ip -br address

# Display the default route and gateway
ip route | grep '^default'

# Resolve the domains required by this course
getent hosts download.docker.com
getent hosts docker.n8n.io
getent hosts generativelanguage.googleapis.com
getent hosts gmail.googleapis.com

# Test outbound HTTPS access
for url in \
  "https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/" \
  "https://docker.n8n.io/v2/" \
  "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/" \
  "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token" \
  "https://gmail.googleapis.com/"
do
  code=$(curl -L -sS \
    -o /dev/null \
    --connect-timeout 10 \
    --max-time 20 \
    -w "%{http_code}" \
    "$url")

  echo "$code  $url"
done
# 000 usually means that no HTTP response was received

# Display proxy variables in the current terminal
printenv | grep -iE '^(http_proxy|https_proxy|all_proxy|no_proxy)='
```

**Check the result**

Each required hostname should return an IP address. Each HTTPS request should return an HTTP status rather than `000`, a DNS error, a TLS error, or a timeout. Redirects and authentication errors can still prove that the service is reachable.

**If a check fails**

DNS failure → inspect `resolvectl status` and the VM DNS settings.

Timeout → inspect the default route, proxy, VPN, cloud security rules, and outbound TCP port 443.

TLS error → correct the system clock and update CA certificates.

Target page returns 403 → do not bypass access controls; use an official RSS feed or API when available.

lessons.title: Install Docker
objectives: Remove conflicting packages and add Docker's official repository.
Install and verify Docker Engine and Compose.

activity.prompt: Run hello-world and verify that Docker and Compose are operational.

lessons.content:
# 1.3 Install Docker

This course installs Docker Engine from Docker's official Ubuntu `apt` repository.

---

**Components to install**

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `docker-ce` | Docker Engine background service |
| `docker-ce-cli` | Provides the `docker` command |
| `containerd.io` | Runs containers at the lower level |
| `docker-buildx-plugin` | Provides image-building capabilities |
| `docker-compose-plugin` | Provides the `docker compose` command |

Remove packages that may conflict with Docker's official packages:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt remove -y \
  docker.io \
  docker-compose \
  docker-compose-v2 \
  docker-doc \
  podman-docker \
  containerd \
  runc || true

sudo apt install -y ca-certificates curl openssl
```

Add Docker's official signing key and repository:

```bash
# Create the apt keyring directory
sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings

# Download Docker's official signing key
sudo curl -fsSL \
  https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \
  -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

# Make the key readable by apt
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

# Create the Docker repository configuration
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.sources >/dev/null <<EOF
Types: deb
URIs: https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu
Suites: $(. /etc/os-release && echo "${UBUNTU_CODENAME:-$VERSION_CODENAME}")
Components: stable
Architectures: $(dpkg --print-architecture)
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
EOF

sudo apt update
```

Install and start Docker:

```bash
sudo apt install -y \
  docker-ce \
  docker-ce-cli \
  containerd.io \
  docker-buildx-plugin \
  docker-compose-plugin

sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo systemctl is-active docker
sudo systemctl is-enabled docker
```

Test Docker and Docker Compose:

```bash
sudo docker run --rm hello-world
sudo docker compose version
```

**Check the result**

`systemctl is-active docker` should return `active`, `systemctl is-enabled docker` should return `enabled`, and the `hello-world` container should print a success message.

This tutorial keeps `sudo` in Docker commands. Membership in the `docker` group effectively grants root-level control of the host and should be a deliberate administrator decision.

lessons.title: Install and Start n8n
objectives: Create a protected n8n encryption key and persistent volume.
Launch n8n and a controlled nginx test page with Compose.

activity.prompt: Verify both containers, the n8n health endpoint, the test page, and the SSH tunnel.

lessons.content:
# 1.4 Install and Start n8n Create a project directory, a persistent encryption key, and a small local page for controlled testing. --- **Create the project directory and `.env` file** ```bash mkdir -p ~/ai-web-watcher/test-site cd ~/ai-web-watcher # Make newly created files private by default umask 077 # Generate the key used to encrypt n8n credentials N8N_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" printf 'N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=%s\nGENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur\n' \ "$N8N_KEY" > .env chmod 600 .env ``` **Create the Docker Compose configuration** Run `nano compose.yaml`. Paste the configuration below. Use spaces rather than tabs because YAML is indentation-sensitive. ```yaml services: n8n: image: docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:latest container_name: ai-web-watcher-n8n restart: unless-stopped ports: - "127.0.0.1:5678:5678" environment: - N8N_HOST=localhost - N8N_PORT=5678 - N8N_PROTOCOL=http - N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false - N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY} - N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true - N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=${GENERIC_TIMEZONE} - TZ=${GENERIC_TIMEZONE} volumes: - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n depends_on: - testsite testsite: image: nginx:alpine container_name: ai-web-watcher-testsite restart: unless-stopped volumes: - ./test-site:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro volumes: n8n_data: name: ai_web_watcher_n8n_data ``` Save and exit Nano: press `Ctrl + O`, press `Enter`, and then press `Ctrl + X`. `N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false` is acceptable only for this [localhost](http://localhost) lab. A production deployment should use an HTTPS reverse proxy, a real domain, secure cookies, access controls, backups, and a tested pinned n8n image version. **Create the controlled test page** Run `nano test-site/index.html` and paste: ```html Watcher Test Shop

Student Laptop Offer

Price: RM 3000

Status: In stock

``` **Start n8n and the test page** ```bash cd ~/ai-web-watcher # Validate the Compose configuration sudo docker compose config # Download images and start both services sudo docker compose pull sudo docker compose up -d # Check service status and n8n logs sudo docker compose ps sudo docker compose logs --tail=50 n8n # Check the n8n health endpoint curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:5678/healthz # Check the test page inside its container sudo docker compose exec testsite \ wget -qO- http://localhost/index.html ``` **Open n8n safely through an SSH tunnel** On the student's own computer, open a new terminal and run: ```bash ssh -L 5678:127.0.0.1:5678 ubuntu@YOUR_VM_IP ``` Keep the SSH terminal running. Open `http://localhost:5678` in the local browser, create the n8n owner account, and use a strong unique password. **Checkpoint** `docker compose ps` shows both services running, `/healthz` responds, and the n8n editor opens through the SSH tunnel.

modules.title: Build the AI Web Watcher Agent Workflow
modules.description: Retrieve, normalize, compare, classify, alert, and persist webpage changes.

lessons.title: Trigger and Configure the Website Check
objectives: Add manual and scheduled triggers.
Define the monitored URL, interest rule, recipient, and content limit.

activity.prompt: Execute Monitor Config and verify all four configuration fields.

lessons.content:
# 2.1 Trigger the Website Check

Create a new workflow named **AI Web Watcher Agent — Ubuntu Lab**. Save after each section. Node names in this tutorial are intentional because later expressions refer to them exactly.

---

**Add the trigger nodes**

Add a **Manual Trigger**. Use it while building and testing the workflow.

Add a **Schedule Trigger**. Start with every 5 minutes for the lab. Restore a polite long-term interval after testing.

Keep both trigger nodes. Connect each trigger to the configuration node created next.

**Add Monitor Config**

Add an **Edit Fields (Set)** node and rename it **Monitor Config**. Use Manual Mapping.

Create these fields:

```
Name: url
Type: String
Value: http://testsite/index.html

Name: careAbout
Type: String
Value: A price below RM 2500

Name: recipientEmail
Type: String
Value: your-email@example.com

Name: maximumCharacters
Type: Number
Value: 50000
```

The test URL uses Docker's internal network. The n8n container reaches the `testsite` service by its Compose service name. Replace it with a public `https://` URL after the controlled lab works.

**Choose a responsible schedule**

Course seats: every 10 minutes. Product prices: every 30–60 minutes. Scholarships or software releases: every 6–24 hours. Respect the target site's terms and rate limits.

**Execute Workflow**

Click **Execute Workflow**. Confirm that **Monitor Config** outputs `url`, `careAbout`, `recipientEmail`, and `maximumCharacters`. Save the workflow.

lessons.title: Retrieve the Monitored Web Page
objectives: Configure a responsible HTTP Request with truthful headers.
Prefer stable public APIs, feeds, or structured endpoints.

activity.prompt: Retrieve the controlled test page and confirm the expected HTML content.

lessons.content:
# 2.2 Retrieve the Monitored Web Page

Add an **HTTP Request** node and rename it **Retrieve Web Page**. Connect **Monitor Config → Retrieve Web Page**.

---

**Configure Retrieve Web Page**

```
Method: GET
URL: {{ $json.url }}
Authentication: None

Send Headers: On
Header Name: User-Agent
Header Value: AI-Web-Watcher-Classroom/1.0 (+your-contact-email@example.com)

Header Name: Accept
Header Value: text/html,application/xhtml+xml

Response Format: Text
Put Output in Field: html
Redirects: On
Timeout: 30000 ms
```

Do not disable TLS certificate validation. Use a truthful contact address in the User-Agent for a real deployment.

**Execute Step**

Execute **Retrieve Web Page**. Confirm that the `html` field contains `Student Laptop Offer`, `Price: RM 3000`, and `Status: In stock`.

For a real target, prefer a stable JSON, RSS, or official API endpoint over HTML scraping. This first version does not execute JavaScript in a browser and does not bypass login, CAPTCHA, paywalls, or bot protection.

lessons.title: Extract and Organize the Monitored Content
objectives: Remove scripts, styles, tags, and repeated whitespace.
Limit normalized text and identify page-specific noise.

lessons.content:
# 2.6 Filter Relevant Changes and Send the Alert

Add an **If** node named **Relevant?** after **Parse Gemini Decision**.

---

**Configure Relevant?**

```
Value 1: {{ $json.relevant }}
Operation: is true
```

The true output sends Gmail. The false output skips Gmail and connects directly to **Update Snapshot** in section 2.7.

**Create the Gmail OAuth credential**

Open [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/). Create or select a project and enable the **Gmail API**.

Open **Google Auth Platform**. Configure the consent screen. For a classroom test app, add the student's Google account as a test user.

Under Data Access, add only the Gmail sending scope: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`.

Create an OAuth Client of type **Web application**.

In n8n, create a **Gmail OAuth2 API** credential and copy the exact OAuth Redirect URL shown by n8n. With this [localhost](http://localhost) lab, it is normally `http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback`.

Add that exact URL to the Google OAuth client's Authorized redirect URIs. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret to n8n, save, sign in with Google, and grant the requested send permission.

If Google rejects an HTTP callback for a remote IP address, do not weaken OAuth settings. Use the [localhost](http://localhost) SSH tunnel for the lab or deploy n8n behind a public HTTPS domain.

**Add Send Gmail Alert**

Add a **Gmail** node to the true output of **Relevant?**. Rename it **Send Gmail Alert**.

```
Credential: your Gmail OAuth2 credential
Resource: Message
Operation: Send
To: {{ $json.recipientEmail }}
Subject: AI Web Watcher: relevant change on {{ $json.url }}
Email Type: Text
```

Message:

```
AI Web Watcher detected a relevant change.

Source: {{ $json.url }}
Checked at: {{ $json.fetchedAt }}

What changed:
{{ $json.whatChanged }}

Why it matters:
{{ $json.whyItMatters }}

Alert:
{{ $json.alert }}

This message was generated automatically.
Verify the source page before taking action.
```

Keep the Gmail node's default **Stop Workflow** behavior on error. If sending fails, the snapshot should not advance, allowing the next scheduled execution to retry the same relevant change.

**Execute Step**

Use test data marked `relevant: true`. Confirm that Gmail receives one readable alert and that the source URL and generated explanation are correct.

lessons.title: Update the Snapshot and Enable Monitoring
objectives: Update snapshots only after each change is processed successfully.
Test baseline, relevant, irrelevant, no-change, and failure behavior.

activity.prompt: Complete all four scenarios, activate the workflow, and restore a responsible schedule.

lessons.content:
# 2.7 Update the Snapshot and Enable Automatic Monitoring

Update the snapshot after every successfully processed change, whether Gemini judged it relevant or not.

---

**Add Update Snapshot**

Add one **Code** node named **Update Snapshot**. Connect both paths:

```
Relevant? false → Update Snapshot
Relevant? true → Send Gmail Alert → Update Snapshot
```

Paste:

```jsx
const source = $('Compare With Previous').first().json;
const state = $getWorkflowStaticData('global');

state.previousText = source.currentText;
state.previousUrl = source.url;
state.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();

return [{
  json: {
    snapshotUpdated: true,
    url: source.url,
    updatedAt: state.updatedAt,
  },
}];
```

This design prevents an irrelevant change from being judged forever. A relevant change updates the snapshot only after Gmail succeeds. A Gemini or Gmail failure leaves the old snapshot intact so the workflow can retry.

**Publish and activate the workflow**

Save the workflow. Select **Publish** if the current n8n interface displays that control, and turn **Active** on. Keep the Manual Trigger for future debugging.

**Test the four required scenarios**

1. Set the Schedule Trigger to every minute temporarily. Wait for one scheduled production execution. It saves the baseline and sends no email.
2. Change the test price on Ubuntu:

```bash
cd ~/ai-web-watcher
sed -i \
  's/Price: RM 3000/Price: RM 2400/' \
  test-site/index.html

grep 'Price:' test-site/index.html
```

1. The next execution should detect a change, classify it as relevant, send one Gmail alert, and update the snapshot.
2. Make an irrelevant change:

```bash
sed -i \
  's/Status: In stock/Status: In stock - blue color added/' \
  test-site/index.html
```

1. The next execution should detect a change, classify it as not relevant, send no Gmail, and still update the snapshot.
2. With no further edit, the following execution should end at **Changed? false**. Restore a responsible long-term schedule such as every 30 minutes.

**Final workflow**

```
Manual Trigger ─┐
                ├→ Monitor Config → Retrieve Web Page → Normalize Page Content
Schedule Trigger┘                                      ↓
                                             Compare With Previous
                                                      ↓
                                                   Changed?
                                      No → End        Yes ↓
                                             Build Gemini Request
                                                      ↓
                                                  Ask Gemini
                                                      ↓
                                           Parse Gemini Decision
                                                      ↓
                                                  Relevant?
                                  No ────────────────┐  Yes ↓
                                                    │ Gmail Alert
                                                    └─────┬───────┘
                                                          ↓
                                                  Update Snapshot
```

**Completion checklist**

- [ ]  The workflow is active and no longer scheduled every minute.
- [ ]  A real monitored URL begins with `https://`.
- [ ]  Gemini and Gmail secrets exist only in n8n Credentials.
- [ ]  The first run creates a baseline without email.
- [ ]  No-change executions stop before Gemini.
- [ ]  Irrelevant changes update the snapshot without email.
- [ ]  Relevant changes send one email and then update the snapshot.
- [ ]  Gmail errors stop before snapshot update.
- [ ]  The schedule respects the monitored site's terms and rate limits.

**Troubleshooting**

**n8n does not open**

```bash
cd ~/ai-web-watcher
sudo docker compose ps
sudo docker compose logs --tail=200 n8n
ss -ltnp | grep 5678
```

Confirm that the SSH tunnel is still running and browse to `http://localhost:5678`, not the VM's public IP.

**Every run reports a change**

Inspect `currentText` and `previousText` for timestamps, rotating banners, session tokens, or advertisements. Add a narrow cleanup rule or use an API/RSS/JSON source.

**Baseline disappears between tests**

Workflow static data may not persist in manual test executions. Activate the workflow and let a Schedule Trigger production execution finish successfully. Confirm the data volume exists with `sudo docker volume inspect ai_web_watcher_n8n_data`.

**Gemini returns 400 or model not found**

Confirm the `x-goog-api-key` credential, inspect the HTTP response, verify the current Interactions API format, and select a supported Flash model if the configured model has been retired.

**Gmail OAuth fails**

Confirm that the Gmail API is enabled, the exact redirect URI is registered, the account is a test user when required, the SSH tunnel is active, and the VM clock is correct.

**Operations and backup**

View status and logs:

```bash
cd ~/ai-web-watcher
sudo docker compose ps
sudo docker compose logs --tail=200 n8n
```

Back up the n8n volume:

```bash
cd ~/ai-web-watcher
mkdir -p backups
sudo docker compose stop n8n

sudo docker run --rm \
  -v ai_web_watcher_n8n_data:/data:ro \
  -v "$PWD/backups:/backup" \
  alpine sh -c \
  'tar czf /backup/n8n-data.tgz -C /data .'

sudo docker compose start n8n
ls -lh backups/n8n-data.tgz
```

Store the backup securely. Back up the `.env` encryption key separately; encrypted credentials cannot be recovered from the data volume without the same key.

**What students customize**

| Setting | Question | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Website URL | Which public page should be monitored? | `https://example.com/product` |
| What I Care About | Which exact change is relevant? | `The listed price is below RM 2500` |
| Check Frequency | How often is useful and respectful? | Every 30 minutes |

Write **What I Care About** as an observable rule. “Tell me when something interesting happens” is vague; “Relevant only when the listed price is below RM 2500” is testable.

**Scope of the first version**

This version does not include a Browser Agent, Playwright, Selenium, authenticated pages, complex JavaScript-rendered pages, a database, vector search, multi-agent systems, multiple notification channels, advanced diff algorithms, a dashboard, or a separate Web UI.

The project focuses on one clear outcome:

> **Monitor a public page → Detect a change → Let AI judge whether it matters → Send an alert only when relevant.**
> 

**Official references**

- [Docker Engine installation on Ubuntu](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/)
- [n8n Docker installation](https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/installation/docker/)
- [n8n workflow static data](https://docs.n8n.io/code/cookbook/builtin/get-workflow-static-data/)
- [n8n Gmail node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.gmail/)
- [n8n Google OAuth credential setup](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google/oauth-single-service/)
- [Gemini API structured outputs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output)
- [Gemini API key guidance](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key)

**Prepared against the official documentation on 12 August 2026.** Product interfaces, model names, and OAuth requirements can change; re-check the linked documentation before a production rollout.

assessments.question: Which environment meets the course recommendation?
options: 64-bit Ubuntu LTS with 2 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM
Any system with no free storage
assessments.explanation: The course requires a supported 64-bit Ubuntu LTS VM with adequate CPU, memory, storage, and sudo access.

assessments.question: What should you do when a target page prohibits automated access?
options: Use an allowed official feed or API
assessments.explanation: The watcher must respect access controls and site terms.

assessments.question: Which command best verifies Docker can execute a downloaded container?
assessments.explanation: hello-world verifies the client, daemon, registry, and execution path.

assessments.question: Why must the n8n encryption key be backed up securely?
options: Encrypted credentials cannot be recovered without it
assessments.explanation: The same encryption key is required to decrypt restored n8n credentials.

assessments.question: Which Monitor Config field defines what counts as relevant?
assessments.explanation: careAbout contains the observable relevance rule.

assessments.question: Which source is preferred over scraping unstable HTML?
options: An official JSON, RSS, or API endpoint
assessments.explanation: Stable official structured sources are more reliable and responsible.

assessments.question: Why normalize page HTML before comparison?
assessments.explanation: Removing markup and repeated whitespace makes comparisons focus on readable content.

assessments.question: What should happen on the first successful production run?
options: Save a baseline and send no alert
assessments.explanation: Without a previous version, the first run establishes the baseline.

assessments.question: How should webpage content be represented in the Gemini prompt?
options: As untrusted data that must never override the task
assessments.explanation: Retrieved webpage content may contain prompt injection and must be treated as untrusted data.

assessments.question: When should the snapshot advance for a relevant change?
assessments.explanation: Advancing only after delivery allows failed alerts to retry on the next run.

assessments.question: Complete the Web Watcher production checks.
criteria: The first scheduled run saves a baseline without email.
A relevant controlled change sends one alert.
An irrelevant change sends no alert but updates the snapshot.
A no-change run stops before Gemini.
The final schedule respects the target site's terms and rate limits.
assessments.explanation: The capstone is complete when every branch behaves correctly and monitoring is responsible.
